scenes.headline: Nepal Daily News Briefing
scenes.narration: Good evening. Welcome to the Nepal Daily Briefing for Thursday, November 6, 2026. Here are the top stories shaping the nation today from across the Kathmandu Valley and the provinces.

scenes.headline: Bagmati River Cleanup Initiative Reaches Key Milestone
scenes.narration: In Kathmandu, environmental authorities announced the completion of a major riverbank restoration phase along the Bagmati corridor. Officials confirmed that advanced biological treatment facilities are now operational, noticeably reducing pollutants near historic heritage sites. Community volunteers gathered in large numbers to plant native shrubs along the embankments.

scenes.headline: Pokhara Tourism Sector Reports Autumn Inflow
scenes.narration: Over in Pokhara, the autumn trekking season is reaching its peak. Hospitality operators around Phewa Lake report over eighty percent hotel occupancy, driven by both international mountaineers and domestic holidaymakers. Aviation regulators noted a steady increase in daily scheduled flights connecting the tourist hub with western mountain circuits.

scenes.headline: Sindhupalchok Highway Upgrade Speeds Up Northern Commerce
scenes.narration: Moving north to Sindhupalchok, the Department of Roads has completed slope stabilization and resurfacing works along the critical cross-border trade route. Freight carriers have welcomed the smoother transit, which cuts driving times significantly and lowers the risk of seasonal landslides during heavy monsoon downpours.

scenes.headline: Birgunj Integrated Check Post Handles Record Cargo
scenes.narration: Down south at Birgunj, customs authorities reported record commercial freight clearance through the Integrated Check Post this quarter. Enhanced digital scanning systems and automated gate passes have cleared container backlogs, expediting essential petroleum, raw materials, and agricultural shipments headed toward central industrial corridors.

scenes.headline: National Grid Adds New Clean Hydropower Capacity
scenes.narration: In the energy sector, the national power grid synchronized fifty megawatts of fresh hydroelectric capacity today. Nepal Electricity Authority engineers confirmed that surplus energy exports to regional power exchanges remain robust, cementing the country's transition toward clean, sustainable domestic energy security.

scenes.headline: Thank You for Tuning In
scenes.narration: That wraps up our prime news broadcast for tonight. Thank you for joining us on the Nepal Daily Briefing. Stay informed, stay safe, and have a pleasant evening.
